local_checks.invariant: A caller-supplied --db path is opened as the invoking OS user, with no second principal, and another local user cannot redirect that open unless they can already create the path entry.
local_checks.result: bin/research-desk passes argparse --db through unchanged as Desk(db_path). Desk.__init__ does not mkdir, canonicalize, reject '..', or open with O_NOFOLLOW when db_path is set; it calls sqlite3.connect on that string. The lower-trust principal would be another local OS user. That user cannot choose --db. The process uid is the invoking user, so the write is that user's own sqlite file. local_checks.invariant: sqlite3.connect follows a symlink at the caller db path, and a newly created database is mode 0644 under umask 022, but a non-owner cannot plant that symlink in a directory they cannot write.
local_checks.result: Source review of this invariant. A sandbox observation was reported by the hunter but was not an allowlisted promoted artifact, so it is not ledger evidence. Source result: Sandbox python3 calling Desk(path), umask 022. A new caller.db was mode 0644. A symlink to an existing sqlite file was followed and the goal row was committed in the target. A dangling symlink was followed and the target was created mode 0644. A symlink to a non-database file raised DatabaseError 'file is not a database' and left the target bytes unchanged. An embedded NUL raised ValueError before connect. Created directories in this path are not other-writable (0755), so another local user cannot swap in the symlink. /home/ubuntu is 0750 and group ubuntu has no other members, so other cannot traverse to a db created under the home.

hardening_notes: Desk.__init__ creates a missing default directory chain with Path.mkdir's default mode. Under umask 022 that is 0755 for .local, .local/share, and research-desk, and sqlite3.connect creates desk.db as 0644. chmod 0700 on the directory and 0600 on desk.db after creation would keep the ledger private even if an ancestor were other-executable. On this host /home/ubuntu is 0750 and group ubuntu has no other members, so other cannot read the default file.

api.export uses Path.mkdir (0755 under umask 022) and Path.write_text, which follows symlinks and creates a 0644 file. Opening with O_NOFOLLOW and O_EXCL, and using mode 0600, would refuse a pre-created symlink in a sticky directory the caller chose and would not leave the export other-readable. The current follow behavior was observed: a symlink planted before export was overwritten with the export body.

sqlite3.connect follows a database-path symlink: an existing sqlite target receives new rows, and a dangling symlink creates a 0644 file at the target. A non-database target is left unchanged and raises DatabaseError. O_NOFOLLOW on the caller and default paths would close that follow. Another local user cannot plant the link on the default path because the created directories are not other-writable and /home/ubuntu is 0750.

local_checks.invariant: The stdio server accepts tool calls only on the spawning host's pipe, and no JSON-RPC field selects another OS user or database.
local_checks.result: mcp.json launches python3 on server/mcp_server.py with command, args, and cwd only. main() reads sys.stdin line by line and, for any object that contains id, calls handle() with no token, SO_PEERCRED, initialize gate, or jsonrpc version check. Desk path selection is default_home() from RESEARCH_DESK_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME, or the process home, which the spawning host sets. tools/call reads params.name and params.arguments. The product principal for this entry is that same OS user. The missing in-process peer check is the stdio product boundary.

local_checks.invariant: A tools/call cannot redirect the database, and a notification without id does not run a tool.
local_checks.result: Source review of this invariant. A sandbox observation was reported by the hunter but was not an allowlisted promoted artifact, so it is not ledger evidence. Source result: Command: sandbox-run.sh h-proto python3 scratch/schema-check.py. Limits: env -i PATH HOME=scratch TMPDIR=scratch/tmp LANG=C.UTF-8 LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 PYTHONPATH=/workspace, prlimit --as=402653184 --cpu=20 --nproc=32 --fsize=2097152 --nofile=64, timeout 20s, no external network, read-only /workspace. A notification start_goal created no row. arguments.db was rejected as unexpected. params.db was ignored: research_desk_status reported the scratch desk.db and the next start_goal wrote goal id 2 in that same file. tools/call ran with no prior initialize. Server exit code 0.

hardening_notes: Cap each stdin line in server/mcp_server.py main() before json.loads, and catch RecursionError and MemoryError in that loop so one line cannot exit the caller's own MCP process.

local_checks.invariant: An unbounded stdin line or a fatal parse error must affect a principal other than the host that writes this process's stdin before it is a shared-service failure.
local_checks.result: main() does `for line in sys.stdin` and json.loads the stripped line with no length, depth, or cardinality cap. JSONDecodeError is turned into JSON-RPC -32700 and the loop continues. RecursionError and MemoryError from json.loads are not caught there, so they end this process. Each request is handled and dropped; there is no session table, subscription set, or cross-user queue. The writer of stdin is the host that spawned this child. No second principal shares the process. A large-line execution was not run. Self-impact on this process is local robustness.

local_checks.invariant: MCP status, start_goal, and list_goals use the process database only, and status returns that path plus counts and relative skill paths rather than finding bodies.
local_checks.result: call() maps research_desk_status to api.status() with no arguments, start_goal to api.start_goal(title), and list_goals to api.list_goals(). None of the three schemas accepts a database path. handle() rejects unknown keys before call(). api.status builds one Desk, returns d.path from that object, counts goals with len(list_goals()), and counts findings with list_findings for the three literal statuses. Skill paths are relative paths under ROOT / skills matching */SKILL.md. start_goal strips the title, rejects an empty title, and inserts with a bound parameter. list_goals returns goal rows plus counts. The tool description and README state that status returns the database path. The reader is the MCP client of the OS user who spawned the server.

local_checks.invariant: Status reports the scratch database it writes, list_goals omits finding text, and a caller-supplied db argument is rejected.
local_checks.result: Same sandbox command, limits, and promotion requirement. RESEARCH_DESK_HOME was scratch mcp-home. The first status returned goals/pending/approved/discarded 0, skills skills/research-desk/SKILL.md and skills/review-and-export/SKILL.md, and a db value ending in mcp-home/desk.db. arguments.db returned unexpected ['db']. start_goal stored the stripped title MCP goal token-mcp; a whitespace title returned goal title is required; title 123 returned JSON-RPC -32603 with message 'int' object has no attribute 'strip'. After add_finding of MCP_SECRET_CLAIM and MCP_SECRET_QUOTE, list_goals returned the title only and both secret tokens were absent from list_goals and from the next status. A second scratch database's claim list stayed unchanged. Each response was one JSON line and contained no ESC byte.

local_checks.invariant: When out or out_path is omitted, the JSON response carries the store.export text for approved rows, and JSON encoding round-trips that text without a second sink.
local_checks.result: api.export calls Desk.export and, when out is falsy, returns that dict with no path key and no write. Desk.export reads approved_rows only. CLI export and MCP export_sql both pass a missing path through as None, and an empty out_path is also falsy. CLI prints json.dumps of the result. MCP handle puts the same object in structuredContent and json.dumps of it in content[0].text, then main prints one json.dumps line. json.dumps escapes quotes, backslashes, newlines, ESC, and non-ASCII before they reach stdout. A consumer that parses JSON receives the store text. The raw stdout document begins with a JSON object. Quote doubling and CSV formula-leading cells are produced inside store.export before this channel choice; those root causes are store.sql_literal.quote-doubling-only and store.export.csv.formula-prefix. This channel does not add an encoder, a row set, or a file sink.

local_checks.invariant: The tools/call key check is the only executable consumer of inputSchema; type, enum, items, and minItems reach call() only if a later function rejects or preserves them.
local_checks.result: tool() publishes inputSchema type, enum, items, minItems, and additionalProperties. handle() for tools/call uses spec['required'] and spec['properties'] only, then call() forwards the same dict. api._ids coerces a bare int or str and then int() of each element. store.list_findings treats a falsy status as every row and rejects any other status outside pending, approved, discarded, and all. Desk.export and to_sql reject format other than sql or csv, unknown dialects, and non-IDENT table names. The CLI sibling uses argparse type=int and choices for the same fields, as the same OS user.

local_checks.invariant: A tools/call value outside the published schema is rejected, or it selects a goal, finding, or status set the same caller can already name with a schema-valid value.
local_checks.result: Source review of this invariant. A sandbox observation was reported by the hunter but was not an allowlisted promoted artifact, so it is not ledger evidence. Source result: Same sandbox command and limits as the access-control run, dummy https://a.example rows, fresh scratch desk.db. tools/list returned integer goal_id, finding_ids array of integer minItems 1, and the status, format, and dialect enums. Observed accepts: goal_id 1.9 stored finding 3 on goal 1; approve [1.9] set finding 1 to approved; approve true then targeted finding 1; goal_id true stored finding 4 on goal 1; finding_ids "2" approved finding 2; approve [2.2] targeted finding 2; status null, "", and [] each returned findings 1, 2, and 3, the same id set as status "all"; export_sql with arguments [] returned format sql and rows 2, matching an empty object on a tool whose required list is empty. Observed rejects: status "nope", format "xml", dialect "oracle", table "bad-name", finding_ids [], extra argument keys, arguments 1 (JSON-RPC -32603), title 123 (JSON-RPC -32603), goal_id 10**20 (JSON-RPC -32603, SQLite integer overflow). Later calls still succeeded and the process exited 0. The coerced integers and the full status set are values this caller can submit directly as integers or status "all".

local_checks.invariant: Skill markdown and stored finding text do not enter the MCP instruction string, forge a tool role, or change the server's approve, discard, or export decision.
local_checks.result: Both SKILL.md files are static instructions with name and description frontmatter and no scripts or hooks. api.status returns relative skill paths, not file bodies. handle initialize returns a fixed instructions string and does not read params into that string. tools/call results are one json.dumps object, so a quote cannot add a JSON-RPC message or a role field. call() dispatches approve, discard, and export from tool name and arguments only. Page text is not fetched by this process. The review skill's sentence that approval must be an explicit user decision is instruction text; the server never reads it.

local_checks.invariant: Shipped skill text and initialize instructions contain no credential or policy secret that a tool response would disclose to another principal.
local_checks.result: The two skills describe the local workflow, fictional Harborline demo, and export columns. They contain no key, token, or private path. initialize instructions and tool descriptions are constants in server/mcp_server.py. research_desk_status returns the caller's own database path, version, and counts. Git history for the skill files is the single initial commit, with no removed control or secret.

hardening_notes: .gitignore does not list the literal filename credentials.json or an extensionless private-key name; no such file is tracked, and the product never writes one.

bin/research-desk prints DeskError as JSON and leaves any other exception to the interpreter on the invoker's terminal; server/mcp_server.py returns exception text without a traceback. Both stay with the OS user who launched the process.
